title: Pentagon Orders Military to Prepare for Renewed Strikes on Iran as Trump Weighs Move
excerpt: US Central Command has been told to finalize strike plans targeting Iranian energy, military and nuclear sites — even as Trump publicly rules out attacks before the November 3 midterms.
body:
• The Pentagon has directed US Central Command to complete preparations for possible new military strikes against Iran, according to US officials cited by Axios — but no final decision or attack date has been set.
  • Potential targets include Iranian energy infrastructure, military facilities and nuclear sites, and renewed combat could come before the November 3 US midterm elections or Israel’s October 27 elections, US and Israeli officials said.
  • The order follows weeks of escalating warnings from President Donald Trump — though he also posted this week that the US military “will not attack Iran before the midterm elections,” a statement that sent crude prices down to about $103 a barrel.
  • The pressure point for ordinary Americans is fuel: with the Strait of Hormuz at the center of the standoff, US gasoline is averaging $4.36 a gallon (AAA), and any escalation would push up shipping, trucking, aviation and food costs within weeks.

The order

The Pentagon instructed US Central Command several days ago to finalize preparations for a possible resumption of large-scale combat operations against Iran, Axios reported, citing US officials. The directive did not include a specific date for the start of any attacks, and President Trump has not yet made a final decision.

https://x.com/NSTRIKE1231/status/2108100598960681184

Should large-scale combat operations resume, they are expected to include massive air strikes against Iranian energy, infrastructure and nuclear targets, according to the sources cited by Axios.

“The Department’s task is to develop and present military options to the President.”

— A Pentagon official, quoted by Axios

The election squeeze

US and Israeli officials cited in the reporting said renewed combat could occur before the US midterm elections on November 3 — and possibly before Israel’s elections, expected a week earlier. That timeline makes the military preparations inseparable from politics: a Reuters/Ipsos poll released October 5 put Trump’s approval rating at 32 percent, a record low in the polling series, with the cost of living identified as voters’ top concern.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1qZuqK8WolI

Trump himself has sent mixed signals. In an Axios interview published September 17, he said he was approaching a “big decision” over whether to “annihilate” the Iranian regime or pursue another course. In a Time magazine interview published October 1, he said expanded US bombing of Iran after the midterms was “possible,” adding that the United States had spent months rebuilding its weapons stockpiles. Then this week, he posted on Truth Social that the US military would not attack Iran before the midterms — and crude prices began to drop.

A stalled diplomacy, a growing buildup

The preparations come as diplomatic efforts have stalled. Trump rejected Iran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, saying its terms did not go far enough, while the administration continues to demand major restrictions on Iran’s nuclear program. Vice President JD Vance said this week that Tehran must meaningfully reduce its uranium-enrichment capabilities for Washington to accept a deal; Iran continues to insist on its right to enrich uranium.

The military buildup is substantial. The Wall Street Journal reported last week that between 9,000 and 10,000 additional US troops are expected to arrive in the Middle East by the end of November, as a third aircraft carrier and another Marine expeditionary unit head to the region. If all three carriers remain in theater, it would mark the first time since April that the United States has deployed three carrier strike groups to the region.

The preparations also followed a meeting of Trump’s top national security officials at Camp David — including Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, CIA Director John Ratcliffe, Joint Chiefs Chair Dan Caine, envoy Steve Witkoff and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent — where Axios reported that Iran was a central topic.

Iran’s warning

Tehran is not waiting quietly. Iranian Army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said this week that the country could undertake pre-emptive military operations if necessary, telling the semi-official Fars news agency that Iran had shifted its military doctrine from a defensive posture to an offensive one. Israeli officials, meanwhile, believe renewed US and Israeli combat operations could prompt Iran to retaliate with a major ballistic-missile attack against Israel — Trump has spoken with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu twice in recent days, according to Axios.

What comes next

The conflict, which began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28, has entered its eighth month, disrupting energy markets through fighting and tensions around the Strait of Hormuz. For now, the Pentagon has its orders and the president has his options. Whether the preparations become strikes — before the midterms, after them, or not at all — remains, as the White House puts it, entirely up to Trump.
